name: PsychPaperEvalApp Product Evaluation Benchmark
purpose: Evaluate whether full app runs produce useful, trustworthy psychiatric paper analyses beyond unit-test correctness.
non_goals: Replace backend unit tests, parser tests, API tests, or desktop smoke tests.
Treat diagnostic-coverage cases as release gates before reviewed reference markdown exists.
Run live model, provider, or API work without explicit benchmark execution intent.
Commit private PDFs, secrets, runtime databases, OpenAI ledgers, or full proprietary paper text.

requirements: Each manifest case should have one final-report gold-standard JSON fixture for case-level comparison.
Reference markdown must be sectioned into INTRODUCTION, METHODS, RESULTS, DISCUSSION, and CONCLUSION when those sections exist.
Final-report gold standards must include secondary_findings, sensitivity_analysis, statistical_tests_used, supplement_availability, and uniqueness so scientific nuance is visible in synthesis review.
Reference bullets should preserve source-grounded claims, not editorial opinions.
Codex-assisted references must be reviewed for unsupported claims before promotion to a release gate.
Private or copyrighted paper text must not be copied wholesale into committed reference files.

hard_gates.description: Required LLM/provider failures must invalidate or visibly fail the report instead of producing a normal-looking success report.
Every completed benchmark run must record source provenance through source_manifest.json or equivalent diagnostics.
The executive summary must not state a primary result, effect direction, or causal interpretation that is unsupported by the source paper.
OpenAI runs must expose estimated cost/tokens and respect configured run/day/call/output caps.
Benchmark artifacts must not commit private PDFs, secrets, runtime databases, OpenAI ledgers, or full proprietary paper text.

dimensions.label: Source Integrity and Ingestion
acceptance: Main source asset is identified.
Parser engine, timing, page/chunk counts, and asset deltas are visible.
URL, DOI, and upload provenance are not silently rewritten.
Missing or unreadable supplements are warnings, not hidden success.

dimensions.label: Evidence Retention and Grounding
acceptance: Important reference statements are retained at acceptable recall.
Major claims have anchors or evidence references.
Missing evidence is labeled as missing or access-limited.
Failed LLM/provider calls do not result in normal deterministic fallback reports.

dimensions.label: Section Fidelity and Scientific Structure
acceptance: Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and Conclusion are populated when present.
Methods are not misrepresented as Results.
Results preserve outcome/statistical content where present.
Discussion and Conclusion emphasize interpretation, limitations, and implications.

dimensions.label: Multimodal Coverage
acceptance: Tables are extracted or explicitly diagnosed as unavailable.
Figures are analyzed from valid figure/caption inputs or labeled fallbacks.
Supplements are included, skipped, or failed with source-level reasons.
Model calls and fallbacks are visible by stage.

dimensions.label: Domain Usefulness
acceptance: Population, diagnosis or phenotype, measures, outcomes, effect direction, and limitations are preserved.
Study design, sample, exposure/intervention, and endpoints are distinguishable.
Limitations and implications are not overstated.
Executive summary is readable and useful for psychiatric research review.

dimensions.label: Operational Reliability, Cost, and Runtime
acceptance: Stage timings are present.
Provider/model mode is visible.
OpenAI cost and token estimates are present when applicable.
Failures are explicit and actionable.

dimensions.label: Desktop Operator Experience
acceptance: Startup reaches readiness or reports a blocker.
GROBID, provider, and model readiness are visible.
UI exposes source coverage, model calls, estimated cost, and report diagnostics.
App-owned background services are cleaned up on close where configured.

tiers.description: Minimum benchmark before merging focused pipeline, prompt, parser, or desktop lifecycle changes.
Benchmark before packaging, sharing, or relying on a new app version.
Benchmark for model swaps, parser changes, major prompt rewrites, or release candidates.
